ir.name: builder_gap_topk_pairs_001
ir.intuition: forms preferences only when the objective gap is meaningfully large, then caps to the strongest gap pairs per instance to stay within a pairing budget while focusing learning signal on clear wins
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # Only create pairs when the winner has sufficiently better (lower) objective.
    thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 256))

    # gap[b,i,j] = objective[b,j] - objective[b,i]; positive => i is better than j
    gap = objective[:, None, :] - objective[:, :, None]
    mask = gap > thr

    B, K, _ = gap.shape
    flat_gap = gap.reshape(B, K * K)
    flat_mask = mask.reshape(B, K * K)

    # Select up to top-k highest-gap valid pairs per instance.
    k = max_pairs_per_instance
    if k > K * K:
        k = K * K

    neg_inf = flat_gap.new_full(flat_gap.shape, -1e30)
    scores = flat_gap.where(flat_mask, neg_inf)
    topv, topi = scores.topk(k, dim=1)
    valid = topv > -1e20

    b_idx = valid.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
    sel = topi[valid]
    winner_idx = sel // K
    loser_idx = sel % K

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'gap_topk_pairs', 'gap_threshold': thr, 'max_pairs_per_instance': int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 256))})
